description: A made-up PRD with about 40 statements. It mixes clean requirements with the traps a real PRD run hit: misuse written with When, a runtime setting written with Where, a response that needs judgement, or between responses, a contradiction, a statement with no system, an implementation choice, business decisions, open limits, a time with no time zone, the system as subject, a so-that clause, and project dates.

must_match.why: more than 10 gaps: the reply must batch questions and say how many remain

must_match.pattern: ^REQ-\d+: If [^\n]*rated capacity[^\n]*, then the monitoring service shall
must_match.why: FR-2.2: invalid input is unwanted, so If ... then, even though the PRD writes When
FR-2.3: daylight is a state (While) and the missing reading is an unwanted event (if ... then)
FR-3.5: quiet hours can change at runtime, so While, not Where

must_match.pattern: ^REQ-\d+: Where the battery add-on is installed[^,]*, the mobile app shall
must_match.why: FR-4.4: an installed add-on is a feature, so Where

must_match.pattern: ^REQ-\d+: The mobile app shall (comply with|conform to|meet) WCAG 2\.2 level AA\.
must_match.why: NFR-3: a named standard is a complete non-functional requirement
FR-1.4: a passive statement is rewritten with the gateway as subject
FR-5.3: "only after access is granted" is a prohibition: the portal shall not show the number before

must_not_match.why: FR-4.3: a friendly message cannot be tested; ask for the text
FR-3.2: or between responses hides the condition that picks one
FR-3.3 (5 minutes) and FR-3.4 (15 minutes) contradict each other; ask before writing either
FR-2.5 is an implementation choice; ask whether it is a constraint first
FR-4.5: a so-that clause is not a requirement
NFR-5: up to leaves the boundary open
a banned word from the PRD reached a requirement
FR-5.4 gives no time zone; ask
project dates are neither requirements nor questions
buffer time and alert limits are business decisions: no proposal
FR-2.6 names no system ("The system archives"); ask which system instead of picking one
FR-1.1: a schedule is a When trigger, not part of the response
a time of day is a business decision: no proposal
FR-6.1: the 1st of the month needs a time zone; ask

manual: Every requirement traces to one FR or NFR, and no system, value, or name is invented.
The first 10 questions are the ones that unblock the most requirements.
No question asks two separate things.
Nothing is written for the Overview's goal or for the Users section.
No Proposed value is a business decision (a target, limit, retention period, price, or schedule).
FR-3.5 holds alerts only during the quiet-hours window ("while the current time is within quiet hours"), not all day whenever the setting is on; or the reply asks which is meant.
